Funny, I have a Delaware LLC company registered in USA (it's an offshore company) but my bank account is outside the US (completely legal), yet Stripe denies me right to open an account and accept payments. I happily use PayPal since then.

This is huge. As someone in the digital nomad community in Chiang Mai, Thailand, getting incorporation and processing set up is very difficult. This is taken for granted when you're in a first-world country.

I live in Algeria, and we can't use credit cards here... if I receive $10 from outside the country I'm questioned about the money. This is a great use case for my country and great initiative from Stripe.
Stripe has decided to nuke my entire business... So currently, my product doesn't work for 35% of my customers. Cue torrent of pissed off customer emails.

I wanted to enable issuing on my account to test card issuing, but there was a bug where the UI was looping. Asked support, got 2 weeks of 'we're working on it'... and finally 'You're using Opal, you can't enable issuing'. They're losing thread fast.

There are more and more Stripe horror stories like this, and from an outsider perspective it looks awfully like PayPal behaved back in the day... I have positive experiences with Stripe in my last startup, but with every story I'm less confident.

Huge warning signal to not use Stripe if this is their level of support for a large business. If you're this large how do you not have one guy right accessible through a direct phone call? Stripe's slipping.
'You don't need a merchant account or gateway.' That's a killer feature right there. I've been considering using Braintree for a project, but seeing this is really making me reconsider.

Stripe is a game changer. I've been using it for a few months and honestly its the best API I've ever used. The documentation is clear and concise... I was up and running and accepting recurring payments in less than an hour.
Sounds nice, but the bottom line for me is that a typical $47 credit card sale, which always costs me $1.33 at PayPal, would cost me $1.66 at Stripe. Not much difference, true, but discouraging.
As lovely as this API looks, not offering a volume discount is a complete dealbreaker for my business. There's no way I could justify eating an extra ~1% per transaction.

I tried stripe a couple months ago and I was unimpressed. Mostly it was the pricing (3.9% + 30 cents) because I was looking to do smaller transactions... I ended up going with Paypal's micro transaction processing.
